annotations.text:
The science page, reshaped. Decisions taken: the hub with four subjects, and the AHA map as a live card (option B), drawn into the hub.

All four subject pages are now drawn: Fitness, Movement, Sleep & heart, Body. Each opens with what the app shows, then the studies.

THE BODY PAGE carries your suggestion: every marker under its Body-page section, with the band Verve screens against and how often to repeat it.

THE TEN BLANK INTERVALS ARE NOW FILLED. Six come from a guideline and cite it. One — blood pressure — is a guideline's interval with a single figure of ours inside it, and says which. Three have no guideline interval anywhere: of those only ALMI carries a cadence, shown in grey and labelled as Verve's own rather than invented, while HOMA-IR and waist are given no schedule at all. The note to the right of the Body board sets out each one.

Static mockups, not a clickable prototype. Sample figures throughout.

The ten intervals, proposed with their sources.

SIX FROM A GUIDELINE

HbA1c — every 3 years when normal; yearly from 5.7; twice a year once diabetes is treated and at goal, every 3 months when it is not. ADA Standards of Care 2026, §2 and §6.

Fasting glucose — the same schedule, from the same ADA screening recommendation, which covers A1C, fasting glucose and the 2-hour value together.

ApoB · LDL · triglycerides · HDL — one panel, one interval. Every 4 to 6 years from age 20 at low risk (AHA; USPSTF says at least every 5). After starting or changing lipid-lowering treatment, 4 to 6 weeks — ESC/EAS 2019, and what the 28 days in the file reduces to. Nothing is scheduled once you are at target: the figure usually quoted is yearly, but it could not be confirmed from the guideline text, so Verve schedules nothing there and leaves the cadence to whoever wrote the prescription.

ONE PART OURS

Blood pressure — yearly under 120/80, and every 3 to 6 months once above it and not on drug therapy: both AHA/ACC 2017. The within-a-month figure from 140/90 is ours. The guideline writes its rechecking advice around normal, elevated and stage 1, and gives one month for reassessing someone who has just started treatment rather than for an untreated reading that high; that untreated figure could not be confirmed from the source text. Rather than leave a stage 2 reading on three months, Verve reuses the guideline's own shortest cadence and marks it as our call.

THREE WITH NO GUIDELINE INTERVAL

HOMA-IR — the Endocrine Society puts calculated insulin-resistance indices in research, not the clinic, and no society has ratified a cut-point. So: no schedule. It redraws whenever fasting insulin and glucose are both entered.

ALMI — neither EWGSOP2 (2019) nor AWGS (2019) names a repeat interval. EWGSOP2 asks for periodic reassessment and draws its acute/chronic line at 6 months, and reports 1–2% muscle loss a year after 50, so anything shorter sits inside the noise of a home scale. Six months, labelled as Verve's cadence.

Waist — no guideline names an interval for a tape measure. It costs nothing and takes a minute, so the honest answer is whenever you measure: Verve records what it is given and schedules nothing.

BUILT. retestIntervals is in data/met-thresholds.json, ten entries. Each holds the interval indexed by which band the reading falls in, a separate schedule for a marker being treated, the interval after a treatment change, whether every number in it is the guideline's, and the source.

Each entry also carries a display block — the prose on this page. It is stored apart from the numbers on purpose. The day counts hold the SHORT end of a range, 91 for "3 to 6 months", so a page that worked its wording out from them would quietly narrow every range it quoted. The range is written once, beside the number it was reduced to.

The site writes none of it. It reaches the Body page through lib/markerExplainers.ts and the generated bodyMarkers.ts, which prints a Repeat line per marker and greys and labels whatever is not a guideline's.

scripts/check-retest-display.mjs holds the two halves together: it reads the leading quantity out of each prose string and fails if it does not match the days beside it. It runs in npm run gen:markers and in the test suite, so an interval changed in one place and not the other cannot ship.
